exercise.name: Lever Pec Deck Fly
aliases: Machine chest fly with forearm pads

reference.title: Lever Pec Deck Fly
reference.listing: Video (movement reference only; the page could not be fetched from the authoring environment (gymvisual.com refused the request), so the data sheet was not read and the movement follows the exercise name and standard coaching)

equipment: Pec deck machine (forearm pads on two lever arms swinging about overhead axles)

breathing.pattern: Breathe out as the pads come together, breathe in as they open.
breathing.cadence: About 1.3 s in, short squeeze, about 2 s out

prescription.effort: Stop 1-3 reps short of failure (RIR 1-3, clinical opinion)
prescription.load: Stack load is user-chosen: pick a weight you can close without the back leaving the pad.
prescription.progression: Add reps, then one plate on the stack; slower opening

cues.text: Sit with the back on the pad and the feet flat; upper arms level with the shoulders, elbows bent about 90 degrees, forearms upright against the pads.
Breathe out and bring the pads together in front of the chest by squeezing the elbows toward each other.
Squeeze the chest with the pads together; shoulders down and back on the pad.
Breathe in and let the pads open slowly until the elbows are about level with the trunk.
Feel the stretch across the chest without letting the shoulders roll forward.

mistakes.fix: Set the seat so the upper arms are level with the shoulders.
Press with the forearms and elbows into the pads.
Stop with the elbows about level with the trunk.
Keep the back and head on the pad.

kinematics.norm: From the arms out to the sides to the pads together in front of the chest (clinical opinion)
Held at about 90 degrees, forearms upright against the pads (clinical opinion)
Upper arms about level with the shoulders (clinical opinion)
Each pad swings about a vertical axle lined up over the shoulder joint (clinical opinion)
Machine and dumbbell flys activated the pectoralis similarly to presses in one study (Welsch 2005)
About 1.3 s in and 2 s out (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual #1350, Lever Pec Deck Fly, video (movement reference)
Welsch, Bird and Mayhew 2005, electromyographic activity of the pectoralis major and anterior deltoid muscles during three upper-body lifts (J Strength Cond Res 19(2):449-452)

cautions: Stop if sharp pain, numbness or tingling occurs.
Stack load is user-chosen: start light; the open position stretches the front of the shoulder.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Shoulder discomfort at the open position: set the range limiter so the arms stop level with the trunk.
progressions: Pause 2 s with the arms together.

muscleNotes.pec_r: Prime mover: brings the arm across the body (horizontal adduction) (Welsch 2005 for fly EMG).
muscleNotes.pec_l: Prime mover: brings the arm across the body (horizontal adduction) (Welsch 2005 for fly EMG).
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_r: Helps bring the arm forward and across.
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_l: Helps bring the arm forward and across.
muscleNotes.core: Keeps the trunk on the pad.
